name: Multnomah County
tax_rate: 11.5% combined local rate county-wide (5% retained by cities for stays inside city limits, 1% regional tourism promotion, 5.5% to Oregon Convention Center programs, Regional Arts & Culture Council and the Visitor Development Fund under the Metro/City/County Visitor Facilities IGA), plus 1.5% state
deadline_pattern: No county grant round; TLT is allocated by intergovernmental agreement to Metro visitor facilities, Travel Portland and the Visitor Development Fund
annual_pool: FY2027 adopted budget lists $43,459,986 in lodging and motor vehicle rental tax revenue in the county's pass-through fund; none is open to outside applicants at the county level
notes: Multnomah County collects the 11.5% tax and passes it through under the Visitor Facilities IGA; it runs no grant program. The practical routes for an event are Travel Portland's Visitor Experience Grant (lodging-tax funded, $25,000 to $50,000, for-profits eligible, February deadline) and Travel Portland Event Sponsorships (up to $30,000 for events of 7,500+ in Portland). Both require the project to be in Portland or the Portland Region, so an event in East County should confirm eligibility with grants@travelportland.com.
pool_note: $43,459,986 is the FY2027 adopted revenue for the county's lodging and vehicle rental tax fund (the budget does not separate the two). All of it is distributed by IGA to cities (5% share), regional tourism promotion (1%) and visitor facilities/VDF (5.5%); no county-level competitive pool exists.

name: Lincoln City
tax_rate: 12% city (raised from 9.5% by voters, November 2022), plus 1.5% state; Lincoln County's 10% applies only outside city limits
deadline_pattern: Rolling within the July to June fiscal year; submit at least 60 days before the project starts; applicants notified within 30 days of submission; funds delivered about 30 days before the project start date; applications are considered only after the annual budget is committed
typical_open: July 1 (start of fiscal year); a new criteria/application packet is posted each summer
annual_pool: Not published; Explore Lincoln City reports $57,865 awarded to seven recipients during FY2025-26 with several applications pending (an earlier June 2025 announcement listed $76,511 to six groups); $1,427,865 awarded since 2009
contact: Stephanie Hull, Explore Lincoln City, shull@lincolncity.org, (541) 996-2119; Tyrel Trainor, Explore Lincoln City, ttrainor@lincolncity.org, (541) 996-1272; Kim Cooper Findling, Director, Explore Lincoln City; office (541) 996-1274
notes: Explore Lincoln City is a city department and the official DMO, funded by the city's TLT; its Community Partnership Fund is the city's grant program and is open to nonprofits and for-profits operating in Lincoln City. Awards are decided case by case by Explore Lincoln City staff rather than a committee, so there is no scoring meeting or presentation; a contract with the City follows approval, with 90% paid up front and 10% on the final report. The program favors products that draw visitors from 51+ miles, overnight stays September through May or Sunday through Thursday, longer stays, and stewardship, accessibility and inclusion. Ineligible: in-house marketing campaigns, operating costs, maintenance and cannabis or tobacco products. Nothing located on the 2027 HB 4148 effect.
members_source: No committee; awards are made at Explore Lincoln City's discretion per https://www.explorelincolncity.com/community-partnership-fund/

The Community Partnership Fund is the only slice open to outside applicants: $76,511 announced for 2025-26 in June 2025 (Lincoln Chronicle), with the industry page later citing $57,865 to seven recipients plus pending applications. Pool size is described as limited and varying year to year.

deadline_pattern: Two cycles a year: spring opens about May 1 with a June 30 deadline (EDC vote at its late-July meeting); fall opens about November 3 with a December 31 deadline (EDC vote at its late-January meeting). The December 31, 2026 date is the pattern; the fall 2026 announcement was not located
annual_pool: $125,000 budgeted per fiscal year for the Tourism Grant Program, separate from the Experience Roseburg DMO contract (January 2025 staff memo)
contact: Chrissy Matthews, Community Development Department, cdd@roseburgor.gov, 541-492-6750, 900 SE Douglas Ave, Roseburg, OR 97470; Stuart Cowie, Community Development Director (staff liaison to the Economic Development Commission)
notes: The Economic Development Commission reviews applications twice a year and can approve grants under $5,000 on its own; requests of $5,000 or more go to City Council as a commission recommendation. Grants are typically up to $7,500 (many awards land at $7,499 to stay under the council-review threshold in practice) and fund marketing of tourist-drawing events, visitor services at tourism facilities, and capital improvements that substantially support tourism. The commission favors events between Labor Day and Memorial Day and has denied requests that promote a single private business, a start-up, non-marketing costs, or applicants with missing final reports. Registered businesses are explicitly eligible.

name: Hermiston
tax_rate: 8% city transient room tax (5/8ths of collections feed the tourism/recreation calculation), plus 1.5% state; Umatilla County rate not located
deadline_pattern: Applications open April 1 and close May 31 every year; the Recreation Projects Advisory Committee (TRT committee) hears presentations and scores in mid-June; City Council adopts the awards at its second July meeting; funds reimbursed after receipts for the fiscal year starting July 1
annual_pool: About $125,000 for the 2026 cycle (15% of 5/8ths of the prior year's TRT); $125,000 budgeted in 2025 with $140,750 awarded; $85,000 budgeted in 2024 with $96,845 awarded
contact: Brandon Artz, Director, Hermiston Parks & Recreation, parksandrec@hermiston.gov, 415 S Hwy 395, Hermiston, OR 97838 (Hermiston Community Center)
notes: Hermiston's Request for Project Proposals for Transient Room Tax Funds is a recreation-focused competitive grant: nonprofit status required, projects must be inside city limits, and highest consideration goes to projects that benefit Hermiston through tourism, promotion, marketing and lodging, then to those serving the most participants and showing broad support. A five-member citizen committee hears 10-minute presentations (June 9, 2026, 3 to 7 p.m. for the 2026 cycle) and recommends awards to council, which has approved totals above budget two years running. Sports tournaments, festivals (Melon Fest, Cinco de Mayo, Juneteenth) and sports facilities dominate the awards, and the Parks & Recreation department itself applies for its free community events. Council asked in July 2025 for fuller packets describing each applicant's proposed use and committee deliberations.

presentation.pattern: Invited applicants present to the committee in the second or third week of June, about two weeks after the May 31 deadline (June 18, 2024; June 18, 2025; June 9, 2026)
presentation.format: No more than 10 minutes including questions; bring pictures and illustrations; held at the Hermiston Community Center, 3 to 7 p.m. in 2026

meeting_schedule: Committee meets once a year in mid-June to hear presentations and score; City Council adopts awards on the consent agenda at its second July meeting (July 8, 2024; July 14, 2025)
pool_note: Pool is a formula: 15% of 5/8ths of prior-year TRT, about $125,000 for 2026 (TRT/Tourism reserve was $178,600 with $101,250 projected revenue in 2025). The whole pool is competitive, but the city's own Parks & Recreation department applies and took $27,000 of the $140,750 awarded in 2025; council approved above budget in both 2024 ($96,845 vs $85,000) and 2025 ($140,750 vs $125,000).
